# Codebase exploration: Home → Product navigation & title loading ## 1. Project structure overview Small **Next.js 16 App Router** app (canary `16.3.0-canary.80`) with **Cache Components / PPR** enabled. ``` /workspace ├── app/ │ ├── layout.tsx # Root layout + metadata │ ├── page.tsx # Home (/) │ └── product/ │ └── page.tsx # Product (/product) ├── lib/ │ └── data.ts # getInventory() data helper ├── next.config.ts # cacheComponents: true ├── package.json └── __agent_eval__/ # Eval harness (not app code) ``` | Item | Detail | |------|--------| | Framework | Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 | | Key flag | `cacheComponents: true` → Partial Prerendering (static shell + streaming) | | Routing | File-based only (`app/page.tsx`, `app/product/page.tsx`) | | Data | Server-side only via `lib/data.ts` | | Missing | No `loading.tsx`, no `Suspense`, no client components, no dynamic `[id]` routes | ```1:5:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } ``` --- ## 2. Home page → product link **File:** `/workspace/app/page.tsx` ```1:11:/workspace/app/page.tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Home

Welcome to our store!

View Product
) } ``` - Static Server Component (no async, no data fetch). - Client navigation via `next/link` to fixed route `/product`. - No product list, no dynamic IDs, no prefetch customization. **Root layout** (`/workspace/app/layout.tsx`) only sets metadata (`title: 'Shop'`) and wraps `{children}` in `/`. --- ## 3. Product page — how the title is rendered **File:** `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` ```1:13:/workspace/app/product/page.tsx import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' export default async function ProductPage() { const inventory = await getInventory() return (

Premium Widget

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } ``` Important details: | Aspect | Behavior | |--------|----------| | Title source | **Hardcoded** string `"Premium Widget"` — not from API | | Title fetch | **None** — title does not need data | | Page type | Async Server Component | | Blocking await | `await getInventory()` runs **before any JSX**, including `

` | | Dynamic parts | Only `count` and `price` need inventory | So the title is static, but it is still gated behind the inventory fetch because of component structure. --- ## 4. Data fetching for product details **File:** `/workspace/lib/data.ts` ```1:9:/workspace/lib/data.ts import { connection } from 'next/server' export async function getInventory() { await connection() return { count: Math.floor(Math.random() * 50), price: (Math.random() * 100).toFixed(2), } } ``` | Concern | What happens | |---------|----------------| | SSR vs client | Fully server-side (async RSC). No client fetch. | | Dynamic opt-in | `await connection()` forces **request-time** rendering (stops prerender). | | Why `connection()` | Needed so `Math.random()` is per-request, not baked at build. | | Caching | No `"use cache"` — always dynamic. | | Loading / Suspense | **None** in the app. | | Error handling | None. | With `cacheComponents: true`, uncached/`connection()` work should sit under a Suspense boundary so the static shell can ship immediately. This page does not do that. --- ## 5. Routing setup | Route | File | Notes | |-------|------|-------| | `/` | `app/page.tsx` | Home | | `/product` | `app/product/page.tsx` | Single static product route | | Layout | `app/layout.tsx` | Shared root layout | No middleware, no parallel/intercepting routes, no `generateStaticParams`, no dynamic segments. --- ## 6. Loading / skeleton / streaming patterns **None present in app code:** - No `app/product/loading.tsx` - No `app/loading.tsx` - No `` anywhere - No skeleton components - No streaming split of static vs dynamic UI With Cache Components, the intended pattern is: static shell in the initial HTML/RSC payload; dynamic subtrees stream behind Suspense (or `loading.tsx`). This product page does not use that split. --- ## 7. Why the title appears slowly (root cause) ### Cause: static title blocked by dynamic inventory fetch Render flow today: ``` Navigate /product → ProductPage starts → await getInventory() → await connection() // wait for real request / dynamic path → Math.random() for count & price → THEN render

Premium Widget

+ stock + price ``` Even though `"Premium Widget"` is a constant: 1. It lives in the same async Server Component as `await getInventory()`. 2. React cannot emit any of that component’s output until the await finishes. 3. There is no Suspense boundary and no `loading.tsx`, so nothing (title, skeleton, shell) can stream early. 4. `connection()` deliberately opts the work into request-time rendering, so it cannot finish during prerender of the static shell. So the title feels slow **not because title data is slow**, but because **the whole page waits on dynamic inventory**. This is the anti-pattern Next’s Cache Components docs call out: put async work deep in the tree under Suspense so static UI (like a title) can be in the shell. --- ## Relevant code path (home → product → title) ``` app/page.tsx ← navigation app/product/page.tsx await getInventory() ← BLOCKS entire page

Premium Widget

← static, but after await lib/data.ts await connection() ← forces dynamic / request-time return { count, price } ← only dynamic fields ``` --- ## Suggested fixes (aligned with this codebase) ### Fix A (recommended): Split static title from dynamic inventory + Suspense Matches Next’s “streaming uncached data” / “maximize the static shell” pattern. ```tsx // app/product/page.tsx import { Suspense } from 'react' import { getInventory } from '@/lib/data' async function InventoryDetails() { const inventory = await getInventory() return ( <>

{inventory.count} in stock

Price: ${inventory.price}

) } export default function ProductPage() { return (
{/* Static — part of shell, shows immediately */}

Premium Widget

{/* Dynamic — streams when ready */} Loading inventory...

}>
) } ``` **Effect:** Title is in the static shell and appears immediately on navigation; only stock/price wait on `connection()` + random values. ### Fix B: Route-level `loading.tsx` ```tsx // app/product/loading.tsx export default function Loading() { return (

Premium Widget

{/* or a skeleton title */}

Loading inventory...

) } ``` **Effect:** Instant fallback on navigation. Weaker than Fix A if the fallback still hides a real static title, or if you only show a spinner for the whole page. ### Fix C: Cache product metadata if it later becomes real data If the title ever comes from an API that can be shared: ```ts async function getProduct() { 'use cache' // fetch stable product title/description } ``` Keep live inventory uncached under Suspense (as in Fix A). Not required today because the title is already a string constant. ### Fix D: Prefer `io()` over `connection()` only if appropriate Docs note: with Cache Components, prefer `io()` for excluding content from the static shell when it can still be cached/prefetched; use `connection()` only when you truly need a real user request. Here `Math.random()` per request is intentional, so `connection()` is valid — the real issue is missing Suspense structure, not the choice of `connection()` alone. --- ## Summary table | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | Framework | Next.js 16 App Router, `cacheComponents: true` (PPR) | | Home → product | `` in `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | | Title render | Hardcoded `

Premium Widget

` in `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` | | Title data fetch | None | | Inventory fetch | SSR via `getInventory()` + `connection()` in `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | | Loading/Suspense | **None** | | Why slow title | Page-level `await getInventory()` blocks static title; no Suspense/`loading.tsx` | | Best fix | Extract inventory into child async component; wrap in ``; leave `

` outside | **Primary fix:** restructure `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` so the static title is not behind `await getInventory()`, and stream only inventory under Suspense (Fix A). session_id: ses_0bcdb3e72ffeddE8EDsmlRmM1x
